name: UrbanGems: Beautiful, Quiet, Happy? (London)
description:
Method replication: same task and questions as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (new Google Street View views of London, © Google). Quercia, O'Hare & Cramer (2014, "Aesthetic capital", CSCW 2014, pp. 945–955) ran the UrbanGems crowdsourcing site, where over 3.3K people voted on which of two London street scenes looked more beautiful, more quiet or more happy. Votes became neighbourhood scores ("aesthetic capital"); image analysis found greenery was the cue most positively linked to all three qualities, while broad streets, fortress-like buildings and council houses went with ugly, noisy and unhappy.

What participants do: after consent, one round of 10 London street pairs: 4 on "Which place is more beautiful?", 3 on "more quiet" and 3 on "more happy", drawn at random from 63 images. Then age, gender and whether they live in London.

Analysis as in the paper: score each image by how often it wins (the paper used the share of wins, corrected for opponents), then relate scores to visual features such as greenery, colour and texture.

Differences from the original study: (1) the images are 63 new Google Street View views (2016–2026) from random points in inner London, not the paper's scenes; (2) the original site let people keep voting after the first round; this template asks one round; (3) the background questions are not given in the paper. The earlier version of this template showed 19 photographs cropped from the paper PDF.
